notes.title: Patch 9.6.3 now public
notes.notes: [h3]Dev Build Preview 0.9.6.3 Release Notes[/h3][p]Hello everyone! [/p][p][b]Thank you[/b] to everyone who has played, and is playing, Era One. A special thank you also to those who sent us error reports to help identify and fix issues with the game. [/p][p]This patch addresses many reported problems, mainly (but not exclusively) concerning the Save System. [/p][p][b]Save files created in previous versions[/b] are not 100% guaranteed to be compatible. We decided it was worth keeping backwards compatibility since many save files do work; however, some may not function as intended. As development continues, we’ll try to make breaking changes only when absolutely necessary.[/p][h2]Save System[/h2][list][*][p]Research queues now persist across saves and are restored on load.[/p][/*][*][p]Active construction and research slots are now saved and correctly restored.[/p][/*][*][p]Stronger validation on station blueprints to prevent empty/invalid lists.[/p][/*][*][p]Resolved cases where modules failed to load or overlapped after loading a save.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed construction that could fail to resume after loading.[/p][/*][*][p]Resources, population, and energy should now restore correctly on load.[/p][/*][*][p]Unit and module counters are accurate after loading a save.[/p][/*][*][p]Build Queue UI reflects the correct number of active construction slots after loading.[/p][/*][*][p]Environmental wrecks no longer disappear on load.[/p][/*][*][p]Eliminated repeated “Module constructed” voice lines after loading.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue that prevented save files from being created[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue that caused unit buttons to not refresh correctly after a research had completed (only after load or new game)[/p][/*][/list][h2]Modules & Stations[/h2][list][*][p]Corrected costs when overriding an existing research/blueprint file.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug that allowed recycling to refund more resources than intended[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue that could prevent building on Wing Extenders while under construction.[/p][/*][/list][h2]Units[/h2][list][*][p]When you target a module, units will keep fighting other modules on the same station (no more stopping mid-fight after one module is destroyed).[/p][/*][*][p]Defensive stances periodically check for firing opponents and reassign targets when appropriate.[/p][/*][*][p]Stances (Defensive, Aggressive, Reactive) now add targets and call for help only when enemies are actually detected, preventing unrealistic long-range engagements.[/p][/*][/list][h2]Gameplay[/h2][list][*][p]Warp Destination checks are smarter and considers visible asteroids.[/p][/*][*][p]Asteroids and enemy station now block warps at a distance to avoid collisions.[/p][/*][/list][h2]User Interface & Settings[/h2][list][*][p]Contextual commands are enabled by default.[/p][/*][*][p]Keybinding is more robust: unbound keys are handled gracefully, and overrides persist more reliably across sessions.[/p][/*][/list][h2]Graphics & Visual Effects[/h2][list][*][p]The navigation plane signal if destination is out of bounds only with color (no error message).[/p][/*][*][p]Command Bridge health bar now displays with the correct color.[/p][/*][*][p]The navigation plane correctly updates color based on the current command type (Utility, attack, movement).[/p][/*][/list][h2]Audio[/h2][list][*][p]Music categories switch more smoothly, with snappier combat cues.[/p][/*][*][p]Volume music and sounds are more consinstent and regulated[/p][/*][/list][h2]Performance & Optimization[/h2][list][*][p]Faster, cleaner scene unloads thanks to reduced object lookups and safer null checks.[/p][/*][*][p]Non-essential systems are disabled in the main menu to keep things lean.[/p][/*][/list][h2]Known Issues[/h2][list][*][p]On some Federation-based maps, saving/loading may cause unusual module behavior; we’re investigating.[/p][/*][*][p]Some combination of connections between modules can still break save files, this is being monitored and fixes will be coming as soon as possible.[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Official early access release to July 25
notes.notes:
Hello everyone,

We are postponing the release of Era One to July.

The game is essentially ready, but we want to make sure everything works properly, so we have extended the project funding until that date. 

Additionally, we have hired a person dedicated to the multiplayer aspect, so it will be possible to play Era One with multiple players from the very first public release, which was not initially planned.
We will continue to release playable builds to our backers, the next one in 15 days, and we will gradually extend builds availability to other users.

A gameplay video is also in the works, as well as sending the build to specialized YouTubers.

We are doing meticulous work and want to create a game without compromises, and the delay in release is just to achieve the level of quality we have not yet reached.

Thank you all for the ever-growing interest and support you provide us.
Beghins

notes.title: Era One dev. update
notes.notes:
We want to thank the many of you who are joining our wishlist, day after day, despite our lack of communication. 
We are working hard, and all our efforts are focused on development.

This is our first post, and we waited so long because we wanted to have a clear vision regarding Era One and its development. 
The Kickstarter campaign allowed us to kickstart this ambitious project, and now the team is strong and can reach the goal.

We will release the development build 4 at the end of March, which will introduce Unity's DOTS (data-oriented tech stack) and a complete transition to HDRP (high definition render pipeline). 
Graphics and performance have received a significant 3X boost, compared to our last build. 
We want Era One to keep up with technology, be upgradeable, and stand the test of time.

The build 4 will be playable for Kickstarter backers, and a detailed gameplay video is in the works, showcasing the system's infinite gaming possibilities. 
We also confirm the release date, set between September and October 2024.
Era One will be released in Early Access with "player vs CPU" and "sandbox" modes, followed shortly by the multiplayer support.
The campaign requires more time and budget, so while the game is prepared to handle it, and it's our final focus, it will be introduced in the subsequent release.

We aim for an uncompromising game with the highest quality and detail. 
Therefore, we're limiting content creation to focus on the quality of what currently exists, while reserving time to introduce new features later with proper focus and care.
Era One is developed by veteran modders and passionate players, it is created following the logic of development builds and "always ready to play." 
With a solid foundation, features are introduced and rigorously tested, sequentially. 
The build is our goal, ensuring the game is always playable in different stages of development, guaranteeing fun, evolution, and, above all, deep quality. 
It's our philosophy, and we're confident you'll appreciate being with us for many years.

Thank You,
beghins
